q-127065:
First, the vector equation of the line is 

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 7\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -11 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3t \\ 2t \\ 7t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}7-3t \\ -11+2t \\ 3+7t\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ Therefore, the parametric equations are:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=7-3t \\ y=-11+2t \\ z=3+7t\end{aligned}
$$

q-127078:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-10}{7}=\frac{y-(-8)}{-4}=\frac{z-(-1)}{11},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(10,-8,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨7,-4,11⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}10 \\ -8 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -4 \\ 11\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=10+7t \\ y=-8-4t \\ z=-1+11t\end{aligned}
$$

q-70866:
Remember that the Cartesian (canonical) equation of the straight line that passes through the point $P({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨{v}_{x},{v}_{y},{v}_{z}⟩$, is given by

$$
\frac{x-{x}_{0}}{{v}_{x}}=\frac{y-{y}_{0}}{{v}_{y}}=\frac{z-{z}_{0}}{{v}_{z}}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Comparing the above to our given equation

$$
\frac{x-11}{-4}=\frac{y-(-3)}{5}=\frac{z-(-1)}{3},
$$

we find that our line passes through the point $P(11,-3,-1)$ and is parallel to $v=⟨-4,5,3⟩.$ Therefore, its vector equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =p+tv \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}11 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations are the following:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=11-4t \\ y=-3+5t \\ z=-1+3t\end{aligned}
$$

q-127405:
First, let's find the corresponding vector equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2-6t \\ 1+3t \\ -5+2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-6t \\ 3t \\ 2t\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ r & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -5\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-6 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

where $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

This implies that the straight line passes through the point $P(2,1,-5)$ and is parallel to the vector $v=⟨-6,3,2⟩.$ So, its Cartesian (canonical) equation is given by

$$
\frac{x-2}{-6}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z-(-5)}{2}=t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Simplifying, we reach

$$
\frac{x-2}{-6}=\frac{y-1}{3}=\frac{z+5}{2}.
$$
